misconceptions.description: Believing one strong password reused across accounts is safe
misconceptions.trigger: learner uses the same password for email, school portal, and social media
misconceptions.feedback: If one site is breached, every account sharing that password is exposed. Use a unique password per account, ideally with a password manager.

misconceptions.description: Skipping two-factor authentication because it adds an extra step
misconceptions.trigger: learner declines 2FA to log in faster
misconceptions.feedback: Two-factor authentication blocks most account takeovers even when a password leaks. Turn it on for email and the school portal first.

misconceptions.description: Trusting an email or text because it sounds urgent and official
misconceptions.trigger: learner clicks a link in a message demanding immediate action
misconceptions.feedback: Urgency is a phishing tactic. Do not click the link; go to the official site directly and verify the sender address.

misconceptions.description: Pasting personal or others' private data into an AI tool without checking what it is allowed to keep
misconceptions.trigger: learner enters a full name, ID number, or private message into a public AI tool
misconceptions.feedback: Do not paste identifiers, passwords, or other people's private data into AI tools. Redact or summarize before sharing.
